# v3.15-dev

Documentation and process. No code changes, nothing behaves differently.

## New

- **A `SECURITY.md`** covering how to report a security problem privately
  (please don't open a public issue), which versions get fixes, and — the
  substantial part — how security is kept current: what runs automatically on
  every change, when a full audit is due, and what an audit covers.

- **Audits are now scheduled against a trigger rather than a date.** An audit is
  due when a new authentication mechanism, externally reachable surface,
  privilege boundary, sink or runtime dependency lands, with a lightweight
  review every 25 releases as a backstop. The reasoning is recorded: the decay
  found in the last review tracked how much the product had grown, not how much
  time had passed.

- **A standing security section in the contributor documentation**, plus a
  question in the post-change checklist and the pull request template asking
  whether a change was security-relevant at all — most are not, and the check
  takes seconds.

## Why

The most useful finding of the last full security review was not a bug. It was
that earlier fixes had quietly stopped holding, because they had been written
down as work that was finished rather than as rules that keep applying. This
release turns them into rules, points at the checks that enforce them
automatically, and is honest about the ones no check can enforce — real customer
and product names among them, which remain a human responsibility.
